source.method: All 80 layout templates classified by authoring model; section sequences for EVERY composed page type derived from the `content_blocks` of every English page; creatable types cross-checked against the 64 CloudCannon collections and 23 creation schemas.

authoringModels.blocks: The whole page is an ordered content_blocks array of Bookshop components. Any section can be added, removed or reordered by editing front matter. Scenes drop straight in.
authoringModels.blocks-in-template: A fixed template (breadcrumb, listing, related items, pricing tables) with a content_blocks region inside it. Blocks can be added, but the surrounding chrome is template-owned and cannot be changed from content.
authoringModels.hybrid-legacy: Renders content_blocks when the page has them; otherwise falls back to a hardcoded legacy template driven by heroTitle/benefits/faqList. ALWAYS author the blocks branch. Never author the legacy branch.
authoringModels.params: A fixed template driven by named front-matter fields. Structure cannot be changed from content. A new section, or a scene, needs a dev-team template change.
authoringModels.body: A markdown body page (plus a few front-matter fields). Prose, not composed sections.

scenePlacement.blocks: direct — add a scene component block, or put the scene in an existing component's image slot
scenePlacement.blocks-in-template: direct, inside the blocks region only
scenePlacement.hybrid-legacy: direct, on the blocks branch only
scenePlacement.params: NOT directly. The scene can only replace an existing image field, and only if the dev team adds a component. Flag as a kit gap.
scenePlacement.body: NOT directly. A scene in prose needs a shortcode the dev team must add. Flag as a kit gap.

howStructureIsDefined: A composed page's sections are the ordered content_blocks array in its YAML front matter, each entry keyed by _bookshop_name; the layout only renders them. Header, footer and promo banners are never blocks — they come from the base layout (themes/optmyzr-marketing-v2/layouts/_default/baseof.html) and its partials.

routing.note: Map the user's words to a pageType key. If the brief does not match any row, say so and ask — never invent a page type.

solution.label: Solution / feature / landing page
solution.alsoUseFor: A generic 'landing page' brief with no conversion form. This is the site's general-purpose marketing page and the default answer unless the brief names something else.
solution.scenes: direct — the primary home for animated scenes

otherLayouts.generic-solutions-page: hybrid-legacy, 34 pages (18 composed, 16 still on the legacy branch)

sections.note: A scene-led page may swap in a bespoke animated hero (sidekick-hero, claude-connector-hero).

sections.frequency: 29/29 v4, 18/18 generic, 4/4 v2 — present on every solution page without exception
14/18 generic, 4/4 v2, only 1/29 v4 — being dropped on newer pages
sections.repeat: one block per case study, up to 3

comparison.label: Competitor comparison / 'Optmyzr vs X' page
comparison.note: 11 of 17 pages use the dominant sequence, 5 the alternate. Read a sibling page before building. The hub page (compare/list.html) is blocks-in-template.

homepage.label: Homepage
homepage.note: 15 blocks, one page. Highest-traffic page - changes need site-owner sign-off.

demo-request.label: Demo request / conversion landing page
demo-request.note: Carries a form. Never touch form wiring or tracking.

product.label: Product page
product.warning: `product-page-template` in .cloudcannon/schemas declares content_blocks but points at generic-product-page, which never renders them. Starting from that schema silently drops every block. Copy amazon.md or social.md instead. For ecommerce, copy one and set data-product to ecommerce.

deprecatedLayouts.generic-product-page: params, 26 fields - every page using it is draft: true
deprecatedLayouts.ca-product-page: params, 32 fields - draft, url ends in /deprecated

product.note: Every LIVE product page is block-driven. The three params-driven templates are used only by unpublished drafts, one of which is explicitly named deprecated, so a new product page should follow the amazon or social sequence and never those.
product.componentReadiness: All 10 components across both sequences are captured. amazon-pricing reads 10 fields the blueprint does not default - set them explicitly.

pricing.label: Pricing page
pricing.note: Only two blocks are authorable. Pricing tables, plan logic and currency handling are template-owned - which is why this type is blocks-in-template, not blocks.

resource-hub.label: Resources / guides / hub pages

content-hub.layout: content-hub — body page with a table of contents
content-hub.warning: The schema declares content_blocks but the layout renders only .Content. Blocks are silently dropped — this is a prose page.

resource-hub.scenes: only in the blocks regions; a scene in prose is a kit gap

blog-post.label: Blog post / article
blog-post.scenes: kit gap — needs a shortcode the dev team must add
blog-post.note: The largest content set on the site. Prose with front-matter metadata; no composed sections.

case-study.label: Case study / customer story
case-study.layout: company/case-studies/single.html — fixed breadcrumb and related-blogs chrome around a blocks region; no markdown body
case-study.note: As prescriptive as the solution page: all four sections appear on all 40 case studies. The template owns the breadcrumb and the related-blogs strip around the blocks.

sections.warning: Template reads `author` and `customerCompany`, which the blueprint does not default.
Template reads `authorCompany`, which the blueprint does not default.

capabilities.label: Capability page (one-click-opt, opt-express, data-insights, campaign-automator, slack-integration)
capabilities.scenes: kit gap — each has its own bespoke template
capabilities.note: Five separate hardcoded templates. Treat as legacy; prefer a v4 solution page for anything new.

legacy-solution.label: Legacy platform pages (google-ads, ms-ads, amazon-ads, fb-ads, yahoo-ads, online-ads, advertisers, data-integrations, custom-solution)
legacy-solution.note: The old /solutions/ tree. Do not build new pages here — use solutions-new with v4.

legal.label: Legal / policy page (privacy policy, terms, DPA, guest-post guidelines)
legal.note: Legal text. Out of scope for this skill — route to the dev/legal team.

misc-one-offs.label: One-off campaign pages
misc-one-offs.note: Each is a bespoke template built for one campaign. Never reuse for a new brief; propose a v4 solution page instead.

notComposedPages.note: 972 of 1117 English files carry no layout key at all — Hugo picks the template from the section or type. These are content entries, not composed pages: 596 blog posts, 41 case studies, 140 PPC Town Hall entries, 47 events, author profiles, archived job roles.
notComposedPages.implication: A brief for one of these is a writing task with metadata, not a page-composition task.
